description: Floating-point numeric-edited PICTURE (the symbol E — a significand character-string and an exponent +9{1..4}, ISO §2023:13.18.40.4 GR13b - introduced 2002. LIVE (data-model design D21 / kb/Work PB66): category numeric-edited, class alphanumeric; the store normalizes the value to a leading-nonzero significand (§2023:14.6.8.4), overflow → EC-DATA-OVERFLOW + the pinned saturated image, underflow → zero (§2023:14.9.25.4 GR6 item 4); the de-editing MOVE, arithmetic GIVING with SIZE ERROR both ways, VALUE, level-88, HIGHEST/LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC. Below 2002 the gate names the edition (0900). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): a 1985 numeric edited item's 'PICTURE character-string is restricted to certain combinations of the symbols 'B', '/', 'P', 'V', 'Z', '0', '9'' ... and the currency symbol (§1985:VI.5.9.4 GR6a) - no 'E'; the 2002 text has 'To produce a floating-point edited result, characters-string-1 shall consist of two parts, separated without any spaces, by the symbol 'E'' (§2002:13.16.38.3 GR12b), and §2002:F.2 item 99 records 'The symbol 'E' can be used in a PICTURE character-string to specify a floating-point numeric-edited data item' (item 7: 'The floating-point type exists both in a numeric form, with a machine-specific representation, and in a numeric-edited form'). 2014 keeps it (§2014:13.18.40.3 GR12b).
